subject: Chemistry
solution:
Key idea: A compound gives a positive iodoform test ($\mathrm{I_2/NaOH}$, yellow $\mathrm{CHI_3}$) if it contains $\mathrm{CH_3CO{-}}$ (a methyl ketone or acetaldehyde), or $\mathrm{CH_3CH(OH){-}}$ (which is oxidised to $\mathrm{CH_3CO{-}}$). Carboxylic acids do not give the test. The test can tell two compounds apart only if exactly one of them gives it.
A. Ethanol, $\mathrm{CH_3CH_2OH}$, has a $\mathrm{CH_3CH(OH){-}}$ unit, so it gives the test. Methanol, $\mathrm{CH_3OH}$, does not. The test can differentiate this pair.
B. Neither $\mathrm{CH_3COOH}$ nor $\mathrm{CH_3CH_2COOH}$ gives the test, because acids are negative. The test cannot differentiate this pair.
C. Cyclohexene has no carbonyl group. Cyclohexanone is not a methyl ketone. Both are negative, so the test cannot differentiate this pair.
D. Diethyl ether, $\mathrm{C_2H_5OC_2H_5}$, is negative. Pentan-3-one, $\mathrm{C_2H_5COC_2H_5}$, is also negative because it has no $\mathrm{CH_3CO{-}}$ group. The test cannot differentiate this pair.
E. Anisole, $\mathrm{C_6H_5OCH_3}$, is negative. Acetone, $\mathrm{CH_3COCH_3}$, is a methyl ketone and is positive. The test can differentiate this pair.
So only pairs A and E can be told apart by the iodoform test.
Answer: (C) A & E Only
